messages.subject: Multiple Level in mirt
parts:
Hi Phil, 

I am trying to fit a 3 latent variable model to a set of questionnaire with 12 items.  The questionnaire has 3 categories for each of the 12 items and for each patient. It looks like below. 

ID    ITEM    CAT1 CAT2 CAT3    PERIOD 
1         1         2        0       .             1
1         2          1        2      0             1
..        ..        

1         12          2       .       2             1
1           1         2         1      0             2 

........
1           12         1         1      0             2 

2         1         1        0       .             1
2        2         2       1     2             1
..        ..        

2         12         .       .       2             1
2           1        1        3     1           2 

........
2           12         1        1      0             2

I wish to fit 3 latent variables to this dataset. In your thought, what is the best way to approach this problem. 

Thanks
Souvik

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Multiple Level in mirt
parts:
Hi Souvik,

mirt uses the long format for fitting models, where each person's responses are expressed on each row. I'm also unsure what you mean by a 3 latent variable model here, because it looks like this is a repeated measures design. I assume you mean that you want a latent variable for each time period?

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Multiple Level in mirt
parts:
I don't follow what you are saying here. The 2PL model is only for dichotomous response formats, so you should not be fitting it to data with multiple response options. Could you provide a sample item format which you are working with? That will indicate the type of polytomous response model that likely should be fitted to the data.

Phil
